ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a 4-bit Binary Adder. The inputs b3, b2, b1, b0 at the upper right are directly connected to one set of 4-bit inputs of the adder. b3 and b2 also branch into a two-input AND gate, and the AND gate output is then connected to the bit corresponding to weight 4 in the other set of inputs of the adder; the remaining bits of the other set of inputs are connected to 0. The adder’s cin is connected to 0, the carry output cout is labeled downward as d4, and the four sum outputs are labeled in order as d3, d2, d1, d0. Reasoning: Let the input four-bit binary number be N=(b3b2b1b0)_2. The AND gate output is k=b3·b2. According to the connection relationship, the adder actually computes D=N+4k, and cin=0; among the outputs, d4 is the carry output of the adder, and d3d2d1d0 are the lower four sum bits. When N<12, b3 and b2 will not both be 1, so k=0, D=N, and the output is d4=0, d3d2d1d0=N. When N≥12, i.e. N=12,13,14,15, b3=b2=1, so k=1, D=N+4=16+(N-12), therefore d4=1, while d3d2d1d0=N-12. This is equivalent to the output giving the quotient and remainder of N divided by 12: d4 indicates whether 12 has been reached, and the lower four bits indicate the modulo-12 remainder. Therefore this circuit performs binary-to-radix-12 conversion.

method.method_draft: Let N=(b3b2b1b0)_2. From the image, define k=b3·b2. The adder computes D = N + 4k, with cin=0, where d4 is the carry-out and d3..d0 are the four sum bits. If N<12 then k=0 and D=N, so d4=0 and the low bits are N. If N≥12 then k=1 and D=N+4=16+(N-12), so d4=1 and d3..d0=N-12. Therefore the output encodes quotient and remainder on division by 12, so the circuit converts binary to radix-12.

method.method_draft: Construct a small case analysis from the observed circuit. For inputs 0000 through 1011, at least one of b3 or b2 is 0, so the AND gate is 0; the adder adds no correction, producing d4=0 and d3d2d1d0 equal to the original value. For inputs 1100,1101,1110,1111, both b3 and b2 are 1, so the circuit adds 0100: 1100+0100=1 0000, 1101+0100=1 0001, 1110+0100=1 0010, 1111+0100=1 0011. This maps decimal 12–15 to one dozen plus remainders 0–3, while leaving 0–11 unchanged. Hence the conversion is binary to radix-12.
